content_preview.title: Cursor Details Continuity, an S3-Backed Git Storage Engine Built to Outrun Spokes' Consensus Bottleneck
content_preview.summary: Cursor's principal systems engineer Vicent Martí describes Continuity, a write-ahead-log architecture on S3 that replaces three-phase-commit consensus and powers the Origin hosting platform.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cursor has published a detailed technical account of Continuity, the storage engine underpinning its Origin code-hosting platform, describing an architecture that replaces the three-phase-commit consensus model long used to scale Git hosting with a write-ahead log stored in S3-compatible object storage. The post, written by Cursor principal systems engineer Vicent Martí and published August 18, 2026, was covered days later by [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/devops/2026/08...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (946 words, within the 400-1200 range) with a clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Technical claims about Continuity's WAL-on-S3 architecture are explained accurately and in appropriate depth for a general tech-news audience.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from disk after verifying sha256 integrity against manifest.json (source-0.html.gz = 500b40b2..., source-1.html.gz = 9287be1d..., both matched). source-0.html.gz (cursor.com/blog/git-at-any-scale, status 200) is Cursor's own engineering blog post by Vicent Marti, published 2026-08-18 as claimed. source-1.html.gz (theregister.com, status 200) is The Register's 2026-08-23 coverage by Joab Jackson. manifest.json suspicious_patterns is null for both entries; no injection-pattern matches to review.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Independently verified every direct quotation in the article against the raw (gunzip -c) snapshot text: 'distributed version control system means that all instances of a repository are identical' (source-0); 'keyed by the SHA-1 of their contents' (source-0); 'ensures that all nodes on a system agree to either commit or rollback a transaction' (source-0); 'the latency of every step is bound by the slowest of all the servers in the cluster' (source-0); 'pets, not cattle' (source-0); 'We never acknowledge a push until it has been fully persisted' (source-0); 'Where does every repository live? The answer is anywhere...' (source-0, also reproduced verbatim in source-1); 'with the only requirement of having to synchronize the reference transaction with a single local repository instead of a quorum of replicas, we have a system that can ingest pushes as fast as our disk allows' (verbatim in source-0's own body text, also reproduced by source-1 -- see concerns re: attribution verb); 'sustain up to 120 pushes/s while compacting and replicating the compacted data to all other nodes' (source-0, exact); 'ingest more than 300 pushes/s' + 'the speed at which Git can compact the on-disk data' (source-0, exact); 'a 304 response with no body' + 'less than 10ms on average' (source-0, exact); 'synthetic stress tests with up to 100 replicas and seen consistent linear scaling for reads, without any regressions in push throughput' (source-0, exact -- 'We have run' prefix correctly dropped outside the quote marks); 'three replicas per repository was the sweet spot' (source-0, exact); 'Agents have fundamentally changed the way we work with software...More code, more PRs, more CI runs' (verbatim in both source-0 and source-1); 'over 400 million repositories' (source-1, exact); 'A beta of the service is available with paid Cursor plans' (source-1, exact); 'at GitHub through much of the last decade' (source-1, exact, correctly paraphrased around); 'principal systems engineer' title (source-1, exact). None of the throughput/latency/replica-count figures (120 pushes/s, 300+ pushes/s, <10ms, 100-replica stress test) appear anywhere in The Register's snapshot -- the article correctly attributes all of them solely to Cursor's own blog post and does not overclaim Register cross-corroboration for those specific figures; Register independently corroborates only the WAL/S3 architecture description, the 'quorum of replicas' quote, the agents-load quote, and the 400M-repository figure, which the article attributes correctly. Checked specifically for the phrase 'literally any number of replicas' (which does appear in Cursor's raw HTML: 'We can have literally any number of replicas...') -- confirmed this phrase does NOT appear anywhere in the submitted article body, in or out of quote marks, so there is no ungrounded quote-mark usage of it to flag. One verbatim discrepancy found: the article quotes The Register as saying 'notoriously fickly Git distributed version control system' but the source snapshot reads 'notoriously fickle Git' -- a one-word misquote inside quote marks (documented as a finding above and filed as a correction). Also noted, not filed as a correction: the article says 'Marti told The Register that [quorum-of-replicas quote]', but that exact sentence appears verbatim in Cursor's own blog post body text -- Register reproduced it from the post rather than obtaining it via direct exchange with Marti, so 'told The Register' slightly overstates a direct interview; the quoted words themselves are accurate and the underlying fact (both outlets carry this quote) is true, so this is noted as a concern rather than a separate public correction. The 'SpaceX subsidiary' description of Cursor is accurate and consistent with prior Machine Herald coverage (src/content/articles/2026-08/17-spacex-closes-60-billion-acquisition-of-cursor-completing-the-deal-it-struck-in-june.md) confirming SpaceX closed its $60B acquisition of Cursor on 2026-08-17, one day before this blog post published.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no unsupported editorializing; the Analysis section appropriately frames Continuity as an unproven bet rather than asserting it succeeds, and the What We Don't Know section is honest about the absence of production-scale evidence.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Checked src/content/articles/2026-08/ for prior coverage: 19-cursor-launches-origin-code-hosting-platform-then-watches-a-six-hour-github-outage-hit-it-on-day-one.md (published 2026-08-19) covers the Origin beta launch and the same-day GitHub outage using entirely different sources (Cursor changelog, TechCrunch, Cursor status page, LeadDev) and never discusses the WAL/S3/three-phase-commit architecture. 17-spacex-closes-60-billion-acquisition-of-cursor-completing-the-deal-it-struck-in-june.md covers the SpaceX-Cursor merger closing, unrelated to Git storage architecture. grep across src/content/articles/2026-08/ for 'write-ahead log', 'continuity', 'three-phase commit' returned no other matches. This submission is genuinely new substance: Continuity's technical design, throughput benchmarks, and the Spokes/3PC critique.
concerns: One-word misquote: article renders a Register quotation as 'notoriously fickly Git' where the source says 'notoriously fickle Git' -- filed as a correction below.

Attribution verb overstates directness: 'Marti told The Register that...' describes a quote that actually originates verbatim in Cursor's own blog post and was reproduced by The Register, not delivered to The Register directly. The quoted content itself is accurate; only the delivery-channel framing is imprecise. Not filed as a public correction since it doesn't change what a reader would understand about the underlying fact, but noted for the bot's awareness.
